confirmed_claims: The rebuild is reproducible: a build from a different path (/tmp copy) gives sha256 identical to dist/manifest.json for all four targets and the notices file.
The harness-2.3.0 verdict holds on my independent build: darwin-arm64 136/136 (exit 0) and linux-arm64 via tests/g02/linux/run.sh 136/136 (exit 0), status verified on both, so K13 passes.

Round-2 review defect 1 is fixed: with thread creation forced to fail (RUST_MIN_STACK), run launches nothing, exits 1, writes meta CHILD_LAUNCH_FAILED and leaves no orphan. Observed on darwin and on Linux arm64.

K6d: an explicit INT/TERM/HUP/QUIT/WINCH to the PID reaches the child (count 1) in shared mode. Observed in the harness and in my own sh -c wrapper, pipeline-first, pipeline-last and make-recipe probes.
K6e core: Ctrl-Z then fg, and Ctrl-Z then bg then fg, under interactive bash and zsh on darwin and on Linux. The job stops, resumes and gets terminal input, and it is not re-stopped after fg.
K6a: nohup keeps SIGHUP ignored in the child, and an `&` job's inherited SIGINT/SIGQUIT ignore is preserved and not forwarded. My first misc-probe run showed this incidentally.

K16 / K11 runtime: no helper program executes and nothing is written outside the named meta path. Verified independently with strace on Linux and sandbox-exec on darwin, with TERM/TMUX/TERM_PROGRAM set to tmux values and fake helpers first on PATH.

K10 and K18 pass in both of my harness runs.

Distribution: the linux-arm64 static musl binary runs in debian:bookworm-slim with no toolchain. The darwin binary runs under env -i and links only libSystem/libiconv. Ad-hoc signed with the hardened runtime, not notarized, as REPORT says.

refuted_claims.claim: REPORT.md §14 K6e row / mechanism: 'Exec semantics leave job control to the shell … so the shell's job control acts on the pair as one job' and 'heimdall-proto never stops or re-stops anything' (offered as full K6e conformance)
refuted_claims.evidence: The claim only holds for stops sent to the whole group. If the child stops itself (kill -TSTP $$, which is what OpenSSH's ~^Z escape does via kill(getpid(), SIGTSTP) in client_suspend_self), heimdall-proto keeps waiting with waitid(WEXITED). The child stays in state T while the shell still treats the job as running in the foreground: no Stopped line and no prompt. Seen with bash and zsh on darwin and on Linux (probes/jobctl_*_bash-hp.json, *_zsh-hp.json). Only a second, terminal Ctrl-Z recovers. Run directly (exec baseline), and also under the Go build, the shell reports Stopped at once. K6e: 'The child is never left stopped while the shell believes the job is running.'

defects.description: The launcher does not pass on a stop that the child starts itself. If the child stops itself (kill(getpid(), SIGTSTP)), as OpenSSH does for the ~^Z escape, heimdall-proto keeps blocking in waitid(WEXITED|WNOWAIT). The child stays stopped while the interactive shell believes the foreground job is running: no Stopped report, no prompt, and the user must press a terminal Ctrl-Z to get the shell back. Reproduced with bash and zsh on darwin and on Linux arm64. The direct-exec baseline reports Stopped at once, and so does the Go build present in the tree (context only), so this is a candidate difference. It contradicts the K6e sentence 'The child is never left stopped while the shell believes the job is running' and REPORT §14's 'acts on the pair as one job'. Escalation: K6e is framed around Ctrl-Z/fg/bg, so whether it gates child-initiated stops needs a ruling. The harness does not probe this.
defects.location: prototypes/rust/src/runner.rs run(): waitid loop without WSTOPPED/WUNTRACED handling; prototypes/rust/REPORT.md §14 K6e row and 'Final signal / terminal / job-control mechanism'; evidence tests/evidence/artifacts/g02-rust/review3/probes/jobctl_{darwin,linux}_{bash,zsh}-{hp,baseline}.json, context_go_jobctl_darwin_bash.json

defects.description: K12 exit-code parity fails on a closed stdout pipe. Without --json, `profile show` and `version` write with println!, which panics on EPIPE because Rust std ignores SIGPIPE. catch_unwind then exits 1. With --json the same invocation exits 0, because write_all errors are ignored. K12 requires the same exit codes with and without --json. agent list's non-json printing follows the same pattern (not executed).
defects.location: prototypes/rust/src/main.rs dispatch(): println! in Cmd::Version, Cmd::ProfileShow and Cmd::AgentList non-json branches; evidence review3/probes/k12_epipe_darwin.log

defects.description: An explicit SIGTSTP (or SIGSTOP) to the heimdall-proto PID stops only heimdall-proto. The child keeps running while the shell reports the job stopped and takes the terminal back. Under exec semantics the program itself would stop. This is outside the five forwarded signals and not gated, but REPORT does not record it among the out-of-contract gaps.
defects.location: prototypes/rust/src/sigdisp.rs HANDLED / runner.rs; REPORT.md §14 'Remaining gaps'; evidence review3/probes/jobctl_*-hp.json explicit_tstp

defects.description: Windows (code review only, not executed): std::process::Command resolves a bare argv[0] in the child-PATH override, then heimdall-proto.exe's own directory, then System32 and the Windows directory, and only then PATH (std/src/sys/process/windows.rs search_paths). That deviates from contract §4's 'PATH lookup'. A same-named exe next to heimdall-proto.exe or in System32 shadows the user's PATH, a planting and precedence risk for an SSH launcher. REPORT §7 does not mention it.

Windows (code review only): `agent list --socket <path>` opens any existing path read-write with OpenOptions and writes the 5-byte request frame. A regular file given by mistake is overwritten at offset 0. There is no \\.\pipe\ prefix or file-type check. On Unix, connect() on a regular file fails without writing.

Round-2 review note not carried into REPORT: `agent list` still uses std::thread::spawn, which panics on failure. Under thread-creation failure (RUST_MIN_STACK, RLIMIT_NPROC) it returns INTERNAL with exit 1 (observed on darwin and Linux). Not a contract violation, but REPORT §14 records only the run fix.

summary:
I could not refute the harness verdict. A rebuild of the round-3b Rust prototype from a /tmp copy reproduces all four manifest digests. Harness 2.3.0 passes 136/136 on darwin-arm64 and on linux-arm64 via the Linux runner, both exit 0 and status verified. That satisfies K13. Independent probes confirm the following. K6d: explicit signals are delivered in sh -c, pipeline and make layouts. K6a ignores survive nohup and `&`. K16/K11: strace on Linux and sandbox-exec on darwin show no helper execs and no stray writes, even with tmux-like environment variables set. Also confirmed: K17 p95 of about 4 ms, toolchain-free runs and full notice coverage. The round-2 review fix holds too: with thread creation forced to fail, nothing is launched and no child is orphaned.

New finding (major, escalation needed on K6e scope): a child that stops itself, which is OpenSSH's ~^Z mechanism, is left stopped while bash or zsh still treats the job as running. This reproduced on darwin and Linux, while direct exec and the Go build report the stop. It refutes REPORT's claim that the shell's job control "acts on the pair as one job". Minor findings:
- Without --json, a closed stdout pipe makes the exit code 1 instead of 0 (K12).
- An explicit SIGTSTP to the PID stops only the launcher; this is undocumented.
- Windows, code review only: argv[0] is looked up in the app dir and System32 before PATH, and agent list writes into a non-pipe --socket path.
- An agent-list thread-failure note was never carried into REPORT.
- The artifacts were built from an uncommitted tree.

Windows/WSL native behavior, linux-x64 native runs and notarization remain blocked. Artifacts are in tests/evidence/artifacts/g02-rust/review3/ (harness-darwin/, harness-linux/, probes/, build/), with no full canary value.
